about.heading: The person behind the code.
bio: Master's degree holder with a double major in project management and full-stack development, I've been coding out of passion since 2013 - games, home automation, web apps - well before making it my job. Today I'm a full-stack developer at a recruitment company.
A permanent role brings structure. Freelancing lets me touch other problems, other teams, and steadily build my own activity, at my own pace.

items.a: Yes, because the framework is clear from the start: defined slots (evenings 7-11pm, weekends), realistic hourly commitments, async communication that never blocks your team. You judge on delivery - clean, regular PRs.

Signed quote before anything starts. Monthly billing for packages, milestone-based for sprints and MVPs. Prices excl. VAT, no hidden costs - third-party services (hosting, licenses) stay under your name and control.

items.q: What if the need exceeds the package?
items.a: We see it coming together: shared, transparent time tracking. Anything outside scope gets a separate quote before being committed to - never a surprise on the invoice.

items.q: Who owns the code? Is an NDA possible?
items.a: The code is fully yours upon payment: delivered to your Git repos, documented, with no dependency on me. NDAs and confidentiality clauses are no problem.

items.q: Do you take over existing code, or only build new?
items.a: Both - and I particularly enjoy existing codebases: legacy takeover, stabilization, and gradual migration are my daily bread. No judgment on the state of the code, we start from wherever you are.
